note: Verified against legislation.wa.gov.au on 2026-08-26. The Rules of the Supreme Court 1971 (RSC) carry their own time rules in Order 3: r 2(1) reckons days exclusively of the first and inclusively of the last day; r 2(2) drops Central-Office-closed days from periods of less than 7 days; r 3 excludes the period between 24 December and 15 January when computing time for filing, serving or amending a pleading or for filing and serving a notice of appeal; and r 4 extends a period that expires on a day the Central Office is closed to the next day it is open (not for documents that must be filed electronically, r 4(2)). The Interpretation Act 1984 s 61 applies to the rules as a written law (s 3(1)) unless a contrary provision applies, and its rollover on 'excluded days' (Saturday, Sunday, public service holiday, bank or public holiday) is what the script models with the WA holiday table; the script approximates Central-Office-closed days with weekends and public holidays, and every computed date carries a warning to confirm the office was open. The Supreme Court (Court of Appeal) Rules 2005 must be read with the RSC (r 3(1)) and pick up RSC Order 3 other than rr 2(2) and 5(3) (r 3(4)). The period rules in this table are Supreme Court rules; the District Court Rules 2005 (consolidation 02-s0-00, current from 20 Aug 2025) and the Magistrates Court (Civil Proceedings) Rules 2005 (consolidation 04-a0-00, current from 2 Jul 2026) carry their own procedural periods and were not verified for this table. The appearance rule stays pending-verification because the operative time is the time stated in the writ itself (RSC O 5 r 11).

computation_provisions.summary: Computation of time for a written law: a period reckoned from or after a specified day excludes that day (s 61(1)(b)) and a period ending on a specified day includes it (s 61(1)(d)); where the time limited for doing a thing expires or falls on an excluded day, the thing may be done on the next day that is not an excluded day (s 61(1)(e)); a number of days not expressed as clear days excludes the day of the first event and includes the day of the second (s 61(1)(g)); 'excluded day' means Saturday, Sunday, public service holiday, and a bank holiday or public holiday throughout the State or in the relevant part of the State (s 61(2)). The Act applies to every written law, including subsidiary legislation, unless express provision is made to the contrary (s 3(1)).

computation_provisions.citation: Rules of the Supreme Court 1971 (WA) O 3 rr 2 and 4
computation_provisions.summary: Reckoning periods of time: clear days are reckoned exclusively of the first and last day, and any other number of days exclusively of the first and inclusively of the last day (r 2(1)); where less than 7 days is prescribed or limited, any day on which the Central Office is closed for business is not reckoned (r 2(2)); where the time for doing an act expires on a day the Central Office is closed and the act cannot be done that day, the time is extended to the day the Central Office is next open (r 4(1)), except for documents required to be filed electronically (r 4(2)). 'Central Office' means the central office of the Supreme Court at Perth (O 1 r 4).

computation_provisions.citation: Rules of the Supreme Court 1971 (WA) O 3 r 3
computation_provisions.summary: In the computation of the time prescribed by the rules or by an order or direction for filing, serving or amending any pleading or for filing and serving any notice of appeal, the period or any part of the period which is between 24 December and 15 January next following is not reckoned unless the Court orders. The table encodes the strict reading (25 December to 14 January not counted); if 24 December and 15 January are also excluded the deadline falls later, so the encoded date is the earlier and safer candidate.

computation_provisions.citation: Supreme Court (Court of Appeal) Rules 2005 (WA) r 3(1), (3) and (4)
computation_provisions.summary: The Court of Appeal rules must be read with the RSC (r 3(1)); where they conflict the Court of Appeal rules prevail (r 3(3)); RSC Order 3, other than rr 2(2) and 5(3), applies for the purposes of the Court of Appeal rules (r 3(4)), so the O 3 r 2(1) reckoning, the O 3 r 3 exclusion for notices of appeal and the O 3 r 4 office-closed extension all apply to appeal periods. 'Working day' means a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in Perth (r 3(1)).

period_rules.label: Memorandum of appearance after service of writ (service in WA less than 300 km from Perth; minimum period)
period_rules.citation: Rules of the Supreme Court 1971 (WA) O 5 r 11(1)
period_rules.trigger: Service of the writ on the defendant; the day of service is excluded (O 5 r 11(4))
warnings: The operative time for a specific defendant is the time stated in the writ (Form No. 1 commands appearance 'within * days after service of this writ on you, exclusive of the day of such service'); O 5 r 11 fixes only the minimum: 10 days for service less than 300 km from Perth, 16 days for 300 km to less than 600 km, 21 days for 600 km and above, the time under the Service and Execution of Process Act 1992 (Cth) for service elsewhere in Australia (r 11(2)), and 42 days for service outside Australia unless the Court orders otherwise (r 11(3)). Take the date from the writ itself. O 12 r 1 governs who may enter an appearance, not the time for doing so.

evidence.note: Verified on 2026-08-26 against consolidation 09-am0-00 that O 5 r 11 fixes minimum periods that must be stated in the writ, not an operative deadline the script can compute from service alone; the entry stays pending and fails closed by design.

period_rules.label: Defence after the later of the time limited for appearing and service of the statement of claim
period_rules.citation: Rules of the Supreme Court 1971 (WA) O 20 r 4(1)
period_rules.trigger: The later of (a) the expiry of the time limited for appearing and (b) service of the statement of claim on the defendant; the responsible lawyer supplies the later date as the trigger
warnings: The 14 days runs from whichever is later of the expiry of the time limited for appearing and service of the statement of claim (O 20 r 4(1)); the trigger date supplied must be that later event, and the time limited for appearing is the time stated in the writ (O 5 r 11), not a date the script can derive.

Where a summons for summary judgment under O 14 r 1 is served before the defence, r 4(1) does not apply unless leave to defend is given, and the defence is then due within 14 days after the order or such other period as the order specifies (O 20 r 4(2)); the Court may give leave to the contrary (r 4(1)) and may extend or abridge time (O 3 r 5), including by written consent for pleadings (O 3 r 5(3)).

A statement of claim must be served with the writ or within 14 days after the defendant enters an appearance unless indorsed on the writ (O 20 r 1); the defence must be filed before the copy is served and the copy served within one working day after filing (O 20 r 3(1)).

O 3 r 3 excludes the period between 24 December and 15 January when computing time for a pleading; the script does not count 25 December to 14 January and refuses if the last day would roll into that window — if 24 December and 15 January are also excluded the deadline is later, so the computed date is the earlier and safer candidate.

Rollover is computed as the next weekday that is not a listed Western Australian public holiday; O 3 r 4 turns on days the Central Office at Perth is closed and does not apply to documents that must be filed electronically (r 4(2)), and Interpretation Act s 61(2) also treats public service holidays as excluded days — confirm the office was open on the candidate date.

evidence.method: Fetched the official consolidated HTML (mrdoc_49048.htm) from legislation.wa.gov.au via the site's RedirectURL agent; O 20 rr 1, 3 and 4 text confirmed exactly and the later-of trigger recorded.

period_rules.label: Appeal to the Court of Appeal from a decision other than an interlocutory civil decision
period_rules.citation: Supreme Court (Court of Appeal) Rules 2005 (WA) r 26(2)
period_rules.trigger: The date of the decision being appealed
warnings: The 21 days applies unless another written law expressly provides otherwise (r 26(2)); an interlocutory civil appeal — an appeal from an interlocutory decision in civil proceedings in the General Division by a judge or master, or under the District Court of Western Australia Act 1969 s 79(1)(b) — must be commenced within 14 days (r 26(1)) and is not computed by this entry.

An appeal is not commenced until the appeal notice and any required accompanying document have been filed and served in accordance with r 27 and rr 28-29; where leave to appeal is required, r 42A applies and this entry does not compute any leave-application deadline.

RSC O 3 r 3 applies to notices of appeal through r 3(4): the script does not count 25 December to 14 January and refuses if the last day would roll into that window — if 24 December and 15 January are also excluded the deadline is later, so the computed date is the earlier and safer candidate. RSC O 3 r 2(2) (short periods) is excluded by r 3(4) and does not affect a 21-day period.

Rollover is computed as the next weekday that is not a listed Western Australian public holiday; RSC O 3 r 4 turns on days the Central Office at Perth is closed and does not apply to documents that must be filed electronically (r 4(2)) — confirm the office was open on the candidate date.
This entry covers appeals to the Court of Appeal only; appeals from the Magistrates Court lie to the District Court under the Magistrates Court (Civil Proceedings) Act 2004 and are not computed here.
